subject.title: fix(config): reject zero-value cron.sessionRetention to prevent silent data loss

question: Should this release invalidate previously accepted zero-duration `cron.sessionRetention` values and rely on `openclaw doctor --fix` to remove them and restore the documented 24-hour default?
rationale: The patch is technically sound and follows repository migration policy, but merging deliberately changes an existing accepted config into a startup/validation failure until doctor repair runs, which is an upgrade-impact choice for maintainers.

options.title: Accept doctor-backed strict validation
options.body: Merge the strict positive-duration rule with the parser-backed doctor repair after the final head is current and required checks pass.

options.title: Defer the validation change
options.body: Pause until the upgrade or startup flow can run the migration without requiring users to invoke doctor manually.

recommendation.title: Accept doctor-backed strict validation
recommendation.body: Merge the strict positive-duration rule with the parser-backed doctor repair after the final head is current and required checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: The session-maintenance unification history most directly connects this person to cron pruning semantics and upgrade behavior.
